newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open mixed in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open mixed in quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mixed in quiet trade on Thursday as investors showed little interest to buy issues ahead of Friday's release of employment data in Canada and producer prices numbers in the United States, dealers said.
"The market is mixed and drifting slightly to the left," said one trader with a Canadian-based brokerage. "There's a lack of interest in a market that is just a little bit tired right now."
"The bill market needs a little bit more weakness before it can attract any real interest," the trader added.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded flat to yield 3.14 percent.
Analysts said consolidation of the Canadian dollar in a range of C$1.3725 (US$0.7285) and C$1.3750 (US$0.7272) did not offset a more bearish tone in the money market.

Canada's dollar opened slightly stronger in light trading on Thursday at C$1.3725 (US$0.7286) amid German hedge fund buying of the unit in overnight trade. But light selling in early morning trade pushed the Canada unit a touch weaker.
The generally bullish sentiment for the currency is not spilling over into the money market, the trader said.
On Friday, Canada will release its labor force survey and the United States will report its producer prices index.
Analysts said both numbers would indicate the extent of economic growth in the two economies.

In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.39 percent from a yield of 3.38 at the close on Wednesday. The one-year T-bill slipped further to yield 3.99 percent from 3.95 percent on Wednesday.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.35 percent, in the upper half of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
